item.title: At a pet shelter
item.description: Name common pets and things used to care for them. Use simple words to say what you do when you visit a shelter.

children.definition: An animal that lives with people and that they look after.
An animal that can bark and that many people keep as a pet.
children.example: The dog is waiting by the gate.
collocations: take the dog for a walk

children.definition: A small animal with a tail and whiskers that can make a meow sound.
children.example: The cat is asleep in the sun.

children.definition: A part that sticks out from the back of an animal’s body.
children.example: The dog moves its tail from side to side.

children.definition: The thick, soft hair that covers some animals.
children.example: This rabbit has soft brown fur.

children.definition: A foot of an animal such as a dog or cat.
children.example: The cat lifts one paw before it moves.

children.definition: A round, open container you can put food or water in.
children.example: There is fresh water in the blue bowl.

children.definition: A long strap that you hold when you walk a dog.
children.example: Please put the leash on before we go out with the dog.
collocations: walk a dog on a leash

children.definition: A space with bars that keeps an animal inside.
children.example: The shelter worker opens the cage to change the rabbit’s water.

children.definition: A tool with many short, stiff hairs, used here to make an animal’s fur neat.
children.example: Use this soft brush on the dog’s fur.

children.definition: To give food to a person or an animal.
children.example: I feed the cats in the morning.

children.definition: To hold something and take it from one place to another.
children.example: Can you help me carry this bag of dog food?

children.definition: A small, soft place for a pet to sleep.
children.example: The dog likes to sleep in its pet bed.

children.definition: A band that a pet wears around its neck.
children.example: The dog has a red collar with its name on it.
